title: Eliminating CPU Cache-Line False Sharing
prompt: A high-frequency Java telemetry ingestion service runs 8 worker threads on an 8-core x86_64 server, each incrementing its own dedicated counter in a shared long[8] array (or adjacent volatile fields in a metrics object) at 100M events/sec. Despite zero locks and zero logical data sharing, CPU utilization spikes to 100% sys/kernel-like stall cycles and total throughput collapses from ~800M ops/sec to ~25M ops/sec. Diagnose the hardware root cause and redesign the counter structure in Java to restore linear multi-core scaling.

spark.summary: When 8 threads increment adjacent slots in a long[8] array, all 8 counters share one 64-byte CPU cache line, causing MESI Read-For-Ownership (RFO) bouncing that collapses throughput from 800M to 25M ops/sec; padding/striping via LongAdder restores linear scaling.
spark.keyTakeaway: Separate per-thread hot counters onto distinct 64-byte cache lines using LongAdder or @Contended padding to eliminate cross-core MESI RFO invalidations.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Modern x86_64 CPUs transfer memory between L1/L2 caches and RAM in **64-byte cache lines**, not individual 8-byte `long`s. A `long[8]` array occupies `64` contiguous bytes—fitting **all 8 thread counters on a single cache line**.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts False Sharing on long[8] (1 Cache Line) vs. Padded Stripes (Core 0 (idx 0) -> MESI Interconnect -> Core 1 (idx 1)); Thread-Local L1 Cache Lines via LongAdder / 64B Stride (Core 0..7 -> L1 Cache Line 0 -> L1 Cache Line 1 -> Scraper (100ms)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Switching from `long[]` to `AtomicLong[]` or separate `volatile long c0, c1...` fields does **not** fix false sharing: **Adjacent Heap Layout**: `volatile long` fields in the same. High-frequency Java telemetry engines eliminate false sharing cleanly in JDK 17+: **`java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder`**: Uses internal `@Contended`-padded `Cell` stripes.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Eliminating false sharing is a staple of low-latency infrastructure: **LMAX Disruptor Ring Buffer**: Padding `Sequence` cursors (`p1..p7`) so producer and consumer heads never share a cache line.

learningJourney.title: Why 64-byte cache-line false sharing kills lock-free scaling
learningJourney.explanation: Modern x86_64 CPUs transfer memory between L1/L2 caches and RAM in **64-byte cache lines**, not individual 8-byte `long`s. A `long[8]` array occupies `64` contiguous bytes—fitting **all 8 thread counters on a single cache line**. Even with zero locks and distinct array indices, every core writing its own `long` must broadcast a **Read-For-Ownership (RFO)** under the **MESI** coherence protocol, invalidating all other cores' L1 caches and collapsing throughput from `800M` to `25M ops/sec`.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Why 64-byte cache-line false sharing kills lock-free scaling works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: What happens during MESI RFO cache-line ping-ponging
learningJourney.explanation:
When Core 0 writes `counters[0]` and Core 1 writes `counters[1]` concurrently:

1. **Cache-Line Ownership Theft**: Core 0 transitions the shared 64-byte line to `Modified`, invalidating Core 1's copy.
2. **HITM Stall Cycles**: Core 1 stalls waiting to fetch the `Modified` line (`HITM` in `perf c2c`) over the inter-core mesh.
3. **Serialized Execution**: Instead of 8× parallel speed, all 8 cores serialize on one cache line.

learningJourney.title: Naive solution (and why AtomicLong[] or volatile fields still suffer)
learningJourney.explanation:
Switching from `long[]` to `AtomicLong[]` or separate `volatile long c0, c1...` fields does **not** fix false sharing:

- **Adjacent Heap Layout**: `volatile long` fields in the same object sit side-by-side in memory on the same 64-byte line.
- **`AtomicLong` Array Density**: Contiguous `AtomicLong` references/objects can still share cache lines, and `AtomicLong` CAS retries under contention.
learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Naive solution under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Striped LongAdder / 64-Byte Padded Cells
learningJourney.explanation:
High-frequency Java telemetry engines eliminate false sharing cleanly in JDK 17+:

- **`java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder`**: Uses internal `@Contended`-padded `Cell` stripes hashed by thread probe; each thread increments its own 64-byte-isolated `Cell` in `< 5 ns` amortized, and the 100 ms scraper calls `.sum()` to aggregate.
- **Explicit 64-Byte Stride / `@Contended`**: When indexing by fixed worker ID (`0..7`), pad each slot to `64` bytes (stride of `8` longs = `64` bytes, or `16` longs = `128` bytes to defeat hardware spatial prefetchers) with zero JVM flags required.
- **Verification**: Validate with **JMH** + `perf c2c` (`L1-dcache-load-misses` and `HITM` drop by `> 95%`).

learningJourney.title: Where Cache-Line Padding applies in High-Throughput Systems
learningJourney.explanation:
Eliminating false sharing is a staple of low-latency infrastructure:

- **LMAX Disruptor Ring Buffer**: Padding `Sequence` cursors (`p1..p7`) so producer and consumer heads never share a cache line.
- **Metrics & Observability Agents**: `LongAdder` / `Striped64` powering Micrometer, Prometheus, and Netty byte counters.
- **HFT & Telemetry Pipelines**: Per-core statistics arrays padded to 64/128 bytes.
